body:
15 Nov 2026, THREE DEVIATIONS FROM THE ITEM TEXT, built in PR #94 and recorded here so that no later agent 'fixes' the item text back (helper-n31's evidence, the lead's review with the advisor):
1. A playlist ROW IS NEVER PURGED, only its entries (the item said 'purge tombstoned playlists'). Evidence: migrate_from_navidrome finds a source playlist by (owner, source_id) with no deleted_at filter, so a purged row would bring a deleted playlist back at the next bring-over; import.playlist has a foreign key with no cascade; a create retried by a long-offline phone still gets the deleted row. The row holds no ref and about 100 bytes (the ref_gone and ref_merge precedent).
2. An entry tombstone carries its playlist: the feed says {id, playlist, deleted: true}. The bare {id, deleted: true} does nothing on today's phone (encore_writer.dart applyPlaylists skips an entry with an empty playlist before it deletes by entry id; a Dart test on the real saved response proves it). That is why change_log.parent exists (migration 0016). A playlist missing altogether is told {id, deleted: true}, which the phone handles.
3. change_log is NEVER pruned: that, not the 90 days, is what keeps an away phone correct (written in library.changes, tombstone_purge.py, docs/17 and docs/18).
ALSO: an import's counts are stored on the import row at purge time (final_*), because they were computed from the entries; the Encore app never reads GET imports/{id}/entries (checked: no client in the repo does, the Host admin has no page for it). OPEN, filed as N-35: the phone's orphan row after a tombstone (pull() reads gone before changes). Known leftovers: an import whose match work failed stays 'running' for ever and is never purged; an add_entries retried with a purged pe_ id after more than 90 days offline would bring the entry back; deleted playlist rows stay for ever by design.
